raw_text:
Thanks — here’s a 12-week progressive strength program tailored for a 30‑year‑old advanced lifter at 20 weeks gestation, cleared for moderate strength training. It respects the common pregnancy precautions you listed: avoid supine work after week 16, no maximal lifts, avoid Valsalva/straining, monitor intensity (RPE 6–7 of 10), stop with any warning signs, and avoid contact sports. I assume she has experience with barbell, dumbbell, cable and machine work; if equipment is limited I can adapt.

Overview and coaching notes (apply throughout)
- Intensity: Moderate. Work mostly in the 6–12 rep range with occasional heavier 4–6 sets but never maximal single rep attempts. Use RPE ~6–7 (she should be able to add a couple reps if needed). Avoid prolonged breath holding; emphasize diaphragmatic breathing and exhale on exertion.
- Positioning: No supine (flat on back) after week 16. Replace supine bench or floor exercises with incline (45°+) or seated alternatives or side-lying where appropriate.
- Volume/progression: 3 strength-focused sessions per week + 1 optional low-impact conditioning / mobility session weekly (total 3–4 training days). Progress by small weekly increases in load or reps, or add a set every 2–3 weeks. If fatigue increases, prioritize maintaining quality over load: reduce load by ~10–20% or drop a set.
- Pelvic floor & core: Emphasize pelvic floor and deep core activation each session. Avoid traditional heavy valsalva and max abdominal crunches; prefer standing/diagonal/vertical core work and gentle transverse abdominis engagement. Cue for pelvic floor relaxation after activation.
- When to stop/modify: dizziness, shortness of breath out of proportion, uterine cramping, vaginal bleeding, fluid leakage, decreased fetal movement (later pregnancy), chest pain, headache, or uterine contractions — stop and contact OB.
- Recovery: Sleep, hydration (extra fluid), protein intake, and frequent small meals to avoid hypoglycemia. Encourage 7–9 hrs sleep if possible. Rest between heavy sets 2–3 min; for accessory work 60–90s.
- Warm-up/Cool-down: 8–12 min dynamic warm-up every session (light cardio 3–5 min + dynamic mobility/activation), and 6–10 min cool-down with breathing, gentle stretching and pelvic-floor relaxation.
- Monitoring: RPE, any pelvic girdle pain or diastasis recti symptoms. If pelvic girdle pain arises, remove heavy unilateral loading and consult physio.

Program structure (12 weeks) — 3 phases
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Strength maintenance and movement patterning. Emphasis on safety and technique, maintain strength with slightly reduced loads relative to pre-pregnancy 1RMs (about 60–75% of previous heavy working sets).
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Gradual loading and volume consolidation. Slightly increase sets and/or reps; keep intensity moderate.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Fatigue management and maintenance; shift volume if needed to preserve strength and comfort. More unilateral and stability work to address balance changes.

Weekly template (applies each week)
- Day A — Lower focus (strength + posterior chain)
- Day B — Upper focus (horizontal + vertical push/pull)
- Day C — Full-body dynamic + unilateral emphasis
- Optional Day D — Low-impact conditioning / mobility (30–40 min): walking, stationary bike, prenatal pool, gentle yoga, breathing + pelvic floor work

Phase 1 — Weeks 1–4 (objectives: maintain strength, technique, pelvic floor awareness)
Session A — Lower / Posterior chain (example)
- Warm-up: 5 min bike + glute activation (clam, band pull‑aparts) + hip circles
- Goblet or safety-bar box squat (box set to hips-to-parallel): 4 sets × 6–8 reps (RPE6–7). Choose goblet/dumbbell if front rack uncomfortable.
- Romanian deadlift (dumbbell or trap bar): 3 sets × 8–10 reps (soft knees, hinge emphasis). No maximal load.
- Split squat (rear foot elevated optional) or Bulgarian split squat, bodyweight or light DB: 3 sets × 8–10 each leg.
- Glute bridge on incline bench or standing single-leg hip hinge (no supine): 3 sets × 10–12. If supine causes symptoms, do banded standing glute squeeze or quadruped hip extension.
- Farmer carry (light–moderate DBs) 3 × 40–60 m, posture focus.
- Core: Pallof press (anti-rotation) 3 × 10–12 each side; Diaphragmatic breathing + 2–3 pelvic floor squeezes between sets.

Session B — Upper (horizontal/vertical)
- Warm-up: 5 min arm bike or row + band pull-aparts + shoulder circles
- Seated incline DB press (back supported): 4 × 6–8.
- Chest press machine or incline cable press (avoid flat supine): 3 × 8–10.
- Seated cable row or chest-supported row: 4 × 8–10.
- Single-arm DB row (kneeling on bench or chest-supported): 3 × 8–10 each side.
- Lateral raises (light) 3 × 12–15.
- Biceps curl and triceps rope pressdowns superset 3 × 10–12 each.
- Core: Standing anti-extension (TRX or hands on Swiss ball facing forward) 3 × 10; breathing practice.

Session C — Full-body / Unilateral / Mobility
- Warm-up: 5–8 min brisk walk + dynamic leg swings
- Trap-bar deadlift light–moderate: 3 × 6–8 (focus hinge).
- Step-ups (box 6–12 in) 3 × 8 each leg (DBs optional).
- Seated single-arm overhead press (light–moderate) 3 × 8–10.
- Cable or band pull-throughs 3 × 10–12.
- Core/hip: Side-lying clams 3 × 15 each side; Bird-dog (slow controlled) 3 × 8 each side.
- Mobility / breath: 8–10 min of thoracic rotations, hip mobility, and pelvic floor relaxation.

Phase 2 — Weeks 5–8 (objectives: small progressive overload, maintain comfort)
Progression approach: add 1 set to main lift or increase reps by 1–2 per set week-to-week; or increase load ~2–5% if RPE remains comfortable.

Session A — Lower
- Warm-up as before
- Front rack squat (light front or safety bar) or goblet if front rack uncomfortable: 4–5 × 6–8.
- Trap-bar Romanian deadlift or light barbell RDL: 4 × 6–8.
- Walking lunges (DBs) 3 × 10–12 steps each leg.
- Single-leg Romanian or cable hamstring curls (standing) 3 × 10–12.
- Suitcase carry 3 × 40 m each side.
- Core: Modified side plank on knee 3 × 20–30s each side + standing Pallof holds.

Session B — Upper
- Seated machine incline press or DB incline press: 4 × 6–8.
- Seated row (heavy-ish but controlled): 4 × 6–8.
- Landmine single-arm press (or standing DB push press but avoid heavy jerk): 3 × 8–10 each side.
- Face pulls 3 × 12–15.
- Rear-delt fly 3 × 12–15.
- Arm circuit: hammer curls / overhead triceps ext 3 × 10–12.
- Core: Standing anti-rotation chops 3 × 10 each side; breathing.

Session C — Full-body / Power-free conditioning
- Warm-up
- Trap-bar deadlift or kettlebell swings (light, hip hinge focus, no ballistic if uncomfortable): 3 × 6–8.
- Reverse lunges 3 × 8–10 each leg.
- Seated cable chest press or incline push-ups against bench 3 × 8–10.
- Cable rows or single-arm rows 3 × 8–10.
- Glute medius work: band lateral walks 3 × 20 steps.
- Core: Bird dog with opposite arm/leg reach 3 × 8; deep breathing.

Phase 3 — Weeks 9–12 (objectives: maintain strength, reduce fatigue, refine unilateral control)
Adjustments: More conservative progression. Focus on maintaining load rather than increasing. Replace any supine with seated or side-lying. Increase rest if fatigue.

Session A — Lower
- Warm-up
- Box squats (safety bar/goblet) 4 × 6.
- Trap-bar deadlift or single-leg Romanian deadlift 3 × 6–8 each leg.
- Elevated split squats 3 × 8.
- Glute bridge alternative: standing band hip extension 3 × 12.
- Carry: Farmer/offset carries 3 × 30–50 m.
- Core: Oblique cable woodchop low-to-high 3 × 10 each side.

Session B — Upper
- Warm-up
- Seated incline DB press 4 × 6–8.
- Chest-supported row 4 × 6–8.
- Seated single-arm overhead press 3 × 8.
- Band pull-aparts / face pulls 3 × 15.
- Scapular retraction work + rotator cuff 2–3 × 12.
- Core: Standing Pallof + controlled breathing.

Session C — Full-body / Conditioning
- Warm-up
- Romanian deadlifts 3 × 6–8.
- Step-ups or reverse lunges 3 × 8–10.
- Cable or machine row 3 × 8–10.
- Single-leg glute bridges on incline (if comfortable) or standing alternatives 3 × 12.
- Mobility and breathing 10–12 min.

Optional Day D — Low-impact conditioning / recovery (recommended weekly)
- 20–30 min brisk walk or stationary bike at conversational pace (RPE ~4–5), or prenatal pool workout 30 min.
- 10–15 min mobility and pelvic floor work: diaphragmatic breathing, gentle kegels (short holds then relaxation), hip mobility, thoracic rotation.
- If she enjoys yoga, choose prenatal classes that avoid deep twists and supine.

Nutrition and recovery guidance
- Calories: Increase modestly as pregnancy progresses. Follow OB guidance. If weight gain is appropriate, add ~200–300 kcal/day on average above pre-pregnancy maintenance during second and third trimester; adjust based on appetite and weight trends.
- Protein: Aim ~1.2–1.8 g/kg bodyweight (higher end supports strength and fetal needs). Spread evenly through day.
- Hydration: Drink regularly; more frequent sips during training. Avoid overheating — train in a cool environment and avoid high heat/humidity sessions.
- Micronutrients: Continue prenatal vitamins and ensure iron/folate/calcium/vitamin D as advised by OB. If vegetarian/vegan or low iron signs, check labs.
- Sleep and rest: Prioritize 7–9 hours/night when possible. Increase rest days if fatigued.
- Pelvic floor: Avoid chronic bearing down with exercise. Teach gentle cues: inhale to soften, exhale to engage pelvic floor slightly and transverse abdominis; then fully relax. If pelvic girdle pain or urinary leakage arise, reduce impact and refer to pelvic health physiotherapist.

Progression example across 12 weeks
- Weeks 1–2: baseline loads ~60–70% of previous heavy working weights (RPE6).
- Weeks 3–6: increase sets/reps; small load increases 2–5% if comfortable.
- Weeks 7–10: maintain or slightly increase volume; keep RPE below 8. Add more unilateral work.
- Weeks 11–12: focus on maintaining load, more recovery between sets, reduce accessory volume if needed.

Exercise substitutions (pregnancy-safe swaps)
- Flat barbell bench press → seated incline press or floor press on wedge/45° or cable chest press.
- Supine core work (crunches) → standing Pallof, anti-extension holds, side planks on knees, bird-dogs.
- Heavy valsalva lifts → use lighter loads, more controlled tempo, belt optional only with trained breathing and OB approval.
- Barbell back squats if uncomfortable → safety‑bar, goblet, box squats, or split squats.

Sample week (Week 6 example)
- Day 1 (Mon) — Session A Lower:
  - Warm-up, Box squat 4 × 6, RDL 4 × 6–8, Bulgarian split squat 3 × 8 each, Glute banded standing kicks 3 × 12, Farmer carry 3 × 45 m, Pallof 3 × 10.
- Day 2 (Wed) — Session B Upper:
  - Warm-up, Seated incline DB press 4 × 6–8, Seated row 4 × 6–8, Single-arm landmine press 3 × 8, Face pulls 3 × 12, Curls/triceps 3 × 10, Standing anti-extension 3 × 10.
- Day 3 (Fri) — Session C Full:
  - Warm-up, Trap-bar deadlift 3 × 6, Step-ups 3 × 10 each, Seated cable chest 3 × 8–10, Single-arm DB row 3 × 8–10, Band lateral walks 3 × 20, Bird-dog 3 × 8.
- Day 4 (Sun) optional — 30 min brisk walk + mobility + pelvic floor work.

Final important notes for you and your client
- Individualize load and volume by how she feels day-to-day. Some weeks she’ll have more energy; other weeks rest more.
- Coordinate with her OB/midwife if any concerns, changes in symptoms, or if she prefers tighter guidelines for load.
- Document sets/loads and symptoms each session so you can regress or progress safely.
- If you want, I can convert this into a week-by-week worksheet with exact loads as percentages of pre-pregnancy 1RM (if you provide those), or give alternative exercises for limited equipment.

Would you like a printable week-by-week plan laid out in a table or PDF, or load progression based on her specific pre-pregnancy lifts?
